title: Ultrasound Properties in Endophthalmitis: Comprehensive Clinical Echography Guide
summary: A complete textbook-level guide on B-scan ultrasonography and UBM characteristics in endophthalmitis. Covers acoustic features of vitreous exudates, retinochoroidal thickening, dynamic echography, differential diagnoses, acoustic grading, red flags, and surgical pearls.

sections.title: Overview & Acoustic Principles of Ocular Ultrasound
sections.content: B-scan ultrasonography (10 MHz probe) is essential in endophthalmitis when dense media opacities (corneal edema, hypopyon, cataract, dense vitreous debris) obscure direct fundus visualization. Sound waves penetrate optical opacities, producing real-time acoustic cross-sections based on acoustic impedance differences between vitreous exudates, membranes, retina, choroid, and sclera.

references.citation: Dada T, et al. Standardized echography in endophthalmitis. Indian J Ophthalmol. 2008.

sections.title: Retinochoroidal & Scleral Echographic Features
content: Retinochoroidal Layer Thickening (RC Complex > 1.5-2.0 mm): Diffuse acoustic thickening indicating secondary reactive choroiditis and retinitis.
Subretinal & Subchoroidal Exudates: Hyperechoic fluid collection causing localized exudative retinal detachment or serous choroidal detachment.
T-Sign (Posterior Scleritis / Tenon Space Fluid): Fluid accumulation in Tenon space creating an echo-void T-shaped shadow adjacent to the optic nerve head.
Suprachoroidal Hemorrhage/Pus: High-reflectivity dome-shaped non-kinetic choroidal elevations in panophthalmitis.

references.citation: Rathinam SR, et al. Ultrasound evaluation of retinochoroidal complex in ocular infections. Retina. 2019.

sections.title: Standardized Echographic Protocol & Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Perform Standardized Diagnostic B-Scan (Gain 75-80 dB for vitreous debris; Gain 55-60 dB for membrane/retinal distinction).
Step 2: Kinetic Echography - Evaluate membrane mobility on eye movement to differentiate posterior hyaloid vs retinal detachment.
Step 3: Vector Quantitative A-scan - Measure spike reflectivity (% height) and retinochoroidal thickness (mm).
Step 4: Risk Stratification - If retina is attached & debris is mild, perform Intravitreal Antibiotic Injection (Tap & Inject).
Step 5: Surgical Decision - If dense membranes, retinal detachment, or fungal etiology detected, proceed to Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV).

references.citation: Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study Group. Results of the Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study. Arch Ophthalmol. 1995.

sections.title: Ultrasonic Red Flags Requiring Immediate Surgery
content: Concomitant Rhegmatogenous or Tractional Retinal Detachment under dense vitreous opacities
Hyperechoic Intraocular Foreign Body (IOFB) with acoustic shadowing or acoustic comet-tail artifact
Panophthalmitis signs: Scleral thickening with fluid in Tenon space (T-sign) and extraocular extension
Fungal Endophthalmitis pattern: Confluent vitreous abscesses with localized tractional membranes

references.citation: Relhan N, et al. Endophthalmitis: Clinical Features and Visual Outcomes. Curr Ophthalmol Rep. 2018.

sections.title: High-Yield Clinical Pearls for Sound Gain Adjustment
content: High Gain (75-85 dB): Essential to detect subtle, low-reflectivity early vitreous exudates and posterior hyaloid membranes.
Low Gain (45-55 dB): Crucial to eliminate low-level noise and differentiate high-reflectivity retina from surrounding inflammatory vitreous membranes.
A-Scan Spike Height: Retinal spikes reach 100% display height with 100% acoustic reflectivity; inflammatory vitreous membranes show 20-60% reflectivity.
Dynamic Echography: Ask patient to move eye side-to-side; vitreous exudates show smooth wave-like mobility, while attached detached retinas show restricted, steep undulations.

references.citation: Green RL, et al. Standardized ophthalmic echography. Radiol Clin North Am. 1998.

sections.title: Role of High-Frequency Ultrasound & UBM
sections.content: Ultrasound Biomicroscopy (35-50 MHz UBM) evaluates anterior segment structures when corneal edema or anterior chamber fibrin obscures visualization. UBM detects anterior hyaloid face abscesses, ciliary body detachment, cyclitic membranes, occlusio pupillae, posterior capsular rupture, and occult retained foreign bodies in the ciliary sulcus or pars plana.

references.citation: Cheung CMG, et al. Ultrasound biomicroscopy in anterior segment inflammation. Clin Exp Ophthalmol. 2012.

sections.title: Serial Ultrasound Monitoring & Prognostic Value
content: 24-48 Hour Post-Injection B-Scan: Decreasing acoustic density of vitreous dots indicates favorable response to intravitreal antibiotics.
Persistent high-density echo exudates at 48 hours indicates clinical treatment failure and urgency for vitrectomy.
Resolution of retinochoroidal thickening strongly correlates with final visual acuity recovery.
Development of secondary tractional membranes on serial scans warns of impending retinal tear formation.

references.citation: Sridhar J, et al. Serial echography in post-procedural endophthalmitis. Ophthalmic Surg Lasers Imaging Retina. 2017.

sections.title: Landmark Evidence & Clinical Guidelines
content: Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study (EVS): Demonstrated that B-scan is crucial for evaluating posterior segment status when fundus is obscured, aiding in decision between biopsy/injection vs vitrectomy.

AAO Preferred Practice Pattern (2022): Mandates immediate ocular ultrasonography in all suspected endophthalmitis cases with media opacity to rule out retinal detachment, IOFB, or choroidal detachment prior to intravitreal injection.
EURETINA Guidelines (2018): Emphasizes serial B-scan echography as an objective biomarker for treatment response and structural complication monitoring.

references.citation: Durand ML. Endophthalmitis Clinical Practice Guidelines. N Engl J Med. 2017.
